catalog_locator: §2.3 'Sílaba, tono y acento', pp. 6-7; §3.3 'Desplazamiento del acento', pp. 13-14 (PDF pages 12-13, 19-20)
catalog_quote: En cubeo una sílaba consta de (C)V. Contrastan dos niveles de tono, bajo ... y alto ... La sílaba acentuada, (marcada con [ˈ] antes de la sílaba acentuada en los ejemplos fonéticos de esta sección) es la primera sílaba con tono alto en una palabra fonológica. En la mayoría de las palabras cubeas, ésta es la segunda sílaba de la palabra, y el acento primario cae siempre en una de las cuatro primeras sílabas. El acento (equivalentemente, la posición de la primera sílaba con tono alto) es contrastivo, por ejemplo: (19) /kuˈjɑwɨ/ 'me bañé (recientemente)' /ˈkujɑwɨ/ 'corrí (recientemente)'. Además de la diferencia en tono, las vocales acentuadas son ligeramente más largas que las inacentuadas en el habla normal, y significativamente alargadas en el habla enfática. En el resto de este trabajo, no se marca el tono, y el acento sólo se marca cuando no cae sobre la segunda sílaba, es decir, cuan…

audit.recode_to: Keep classification lexical. Refine the primary-stress rule to 'lexically contrastive stress on the first or second syllable of the word (two-syllable left-edge window; proclitics count), weight-insensitive; H/HL word melodies dock on the stressed syllable' and the secondary-stress rule to 'rhythmic secondary stress on heads of iambic feet parsed left-to-right from the primary (Chacon 2012:119,134)', replacing 'None described' and the 'first four syllables' window; cite Chacon 2012 ch.4 as co-deciding source.
audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding quotation is verbatim on printed pp.6-7 (§2.3) and pp.13-14 (§3.3) of the held Morse & Maxwell 2000 PDF, verified from the held 150/300-dpi page render p012 and the held scanned; locator correct. (2) Deciding source is a 1999 SIL reference grammar (Spanish ed. 2000) whose accent statement is brief and defines accent as the first high-toned syllable. Glottolog's best item, Chacon 2012 (376-pp phonology+morphology dissertation, UH Mānoa), was not yet obtained; downloaded now from ScholarSpace together with Chacon 2011 WP. (3) Chacon ch.4 confirms the lexical classification outright ('Stress is lexically contrastive', 'not sensitive to syllable weight', p.111) and confirms our StressTyp2 contradiction note (fn.2 explicitly rejects the Salser/Morse-Maxwell 'first high pitch' analysis, so StressTyp2's F/ 'first heavy = high tone' is an artefact). sources.quote: p.111: 'Every word must be stressed • Stress must fall at most two syllables from the left edge of words • Stress is lexically contrastive • Stress generate a rhythmic alternation ... • Stress is not sensitive to syllable weight'. fn.2: 'Previous analyses on Kubeo (cf. Salser 1971, Morse & Maxwell 1999) described a system where stress predictably falls on the first high-pitched vowel of words ... Such an analysis lacks several details and important data such as the presence of stress in words without tone. sources.locator: ch.4 'Stress and Tones', §4.1.1 p.111 (PDF p.132); §4.1.1 pp.113-115 exx. (4.6)-(4.11); p.119 (iambic rhythm, secondary stress); §4.1.2.3 p.134; fn.2 p.111
sources.note: Glottolog's top-ranked description; dedicated 50-pp stress-and-tone chapter with phonetic measurements that separates stress from tone and narrows the accent window to the first two syllables and documents iambic secondary stress — our record rests on a 2-paragraph statement in the 1999 SIL grammar and codes 'secondary: none described' and a four-syllable window.

sources.citation: Chacon, Thiago Costa. 2011. The interaction of stress and tones in Kubeo. Working Papers in Linguistics, University of Hawai'i at Mānoa 42(2). 23 pp. hdl:10125/73239.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: Abstract: 'stress and tones have independent properties, while at the same time both rely on properties that are relevant to both stress and tones, such as primary accent and iambic feet.' Preliminary version of the dissertation's ch.4 analysis (lexical accent within the first two syllables, iambic secondary rhythm).
sources.note: Compact statement of the same stress/tone analysis; useful as a citable short source alongside the dissertation.
